_doc: Batch 01, Quill at sensors (control room). Formal, measured, dry; 'Captain' as punctuation; corrects, never interrupts; never says anything she isn't sure of; hides the signals until 1.9 (so nothing here names them before knows.unexplained_signals).

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Calibration, in the same order as always.

lines.text: Quill checks her tools in the same order she checked them an hour ago.
Calibration's on the schedule, between the first check and the second. It isn't negotiable, Captain. It isn't personal.
Quill checks her tools in the same order she checked them an hour ago. She doesn't look up.
Sensors nominal, Captain.

source: crew_cards.md: checks her tools in the same order every watch

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: The same meal at the same time.

lines.text: I eat at the same time every day. Nobody finds that interesting until they try to schedule around it.
Fenwick has stopped trying. I count that as the first sensible thing he's done with the galley.

source: crew_cards.md: eats the same meal at the same time

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Castellan has left her a sandwich.

lines.text: A sandwich sits on the edge of Quill's console, with a label.
Castellan's. My name, spelled correctly, which I choose to read as effort.
I haven't asked why. I've eaten it. Those two facts are unrelated.

source: crew_cards.md: Castellan has decided Quill is his friend

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Dace narrates her sleep.

lines.text: Dace has described my sleeping to me. Apparently I 'hold very still.'
That's what sleeping is. I'd have thought a doctor would know.

source: crew_cards.md: shares a cabin with Dace

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Low trust: she hands you a slate instead of talking.

lines.text: Quill hands you a slate rather than speaking. Three lines, each a complete thought.
I find a slate is less of a conversation, Captain. I'd like you to know it isn't a criticism.

source: act1_calls.md: low trust asks by slate

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: High trust: you never ask her to round a number.

lines.text: You haven't asked me to round a number since the first day. I wanted that noted somewhere.
This is somewhere.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: You haven't asked again what she wrote down.

lines.text: You haven't asked again what I wrote down. Thank you.
I'll tell you when it's something I can stand behind.

source: act1_first_morning.md 1.2b: A time. I write down times.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: A tight ship: checklists.

lines.text: The checklist is signed and countersigned. I feel like a person, Captain.
I'm not certain it's good for me.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: A loose ship: someone moves her stylus tray.

lines.text: Someone has moved my stylus tray. I put it back. They moved it again.
I'm treating it as a study. I'll have results by the end of the leg.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Quill keeps the quiet hour.

lines.text: My hour on the bridge is the best of the day. Nobody talks, and the ship still hums.
I've labelled it as mine, so nobody argues.

source: act1_crew_meeting.md: keep it with Quill on watch

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: She won the argument and doesn't like how it feels.

lines.text: I'd like it recorded that I was right about the hour.
I'd also like it recorded that I don't like how it feels.

source: act1_aftermath.md B1: She won that argument this morning

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Ames died: she cannot say more than sensors nominal.

lines.text: Quill has the watch log open to one page. She closes it, squares it to the console edge, and squares it again.
Sensors nominal, Captain. I'd like to say more than that, and I'm not able to.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Ames lived: she chose the word 'wounded' for the log.

lines.text: I wrote 'wounded' in the log. It's a better word than the other one.
I find I look at that page more often than the log requires.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: A signals background: you know what a quiet band sounds like.

lines.text: You know what a quiet band sounds like. That's rarer than you'd expect, Captain.
I wanted you to know I'd noticed.

source: act1_calls.md: player.background = signals pays off with Quill

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: The classifier link: she does not like not knowing where speed comes from.

lines.text: The classifier is faster. I don't object to faster.
I object to not knowing where faster comes from.

source: mini_missions.md: Pell assists cost Quill trust

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: A wrong classification, written in red.

lines.text: One of the last hunt's classifications was wrong. I've written it in red.
It's a good habit. It also hurts, which I suspect is the point.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: After 1.9: her list for hearing the signal from Vesper.

lines.text: Vesper's a long way from here. I've started a list of what I'll need to hear it from there.
It's a short list. Nearly every item is 'quiet.'

source: act1_close.md: I need to hear it from somewhere else, a long way from here

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Murder route: eyes on the console.

lines.text: Quill has her eyes on her console and her hands very still.
No contacts, Captain. The noise floor is normal.

source: act1_aftermath.md C: she doesn't look up at all

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Murder route: she records everything.

lines.text: Quill writes in her log, tilts the page away, and goes on writing.
I record what happens. All of it. That's the whole of my job, Captain.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Murder route: she wants to know the plan.

lines.text: I'll complete this watch. I'll complete the next one.
At some point I'd like to know what you intend for the ones after. I'd prefer to hear it from you.

source: crew_cards.md: Quill wants the truth, including the bad news

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: The decoy's turn, written down three ways.

lines.text: It turned toward us for forty seconds and came back. I've written that down three ways.
I still don't have a fourth, and I'd like one.

storylets.speaker: quill
storylets.summary: Before the audit: she wants the count to match.

lines.text: At Vesper they'll count what we've declared. I'd like the count to match what we've done.
That's all I want, Captain, and it's rather a lot.
